Fantasy Football Analyzer -- Team Roster Season Analysis¶

This notebook runs a full end-to-end roster analysis for one team's season, then applies the exact same analysis to every team in the league and compares the results with visualizations.

"End-to-end" means it exercises the whole pipeline described in AGENTS.md, not just Epic 7: Sleeper client -> LeagueSnapshot -> season matchups -> league analytics (Epic 6) -> the player-week fact table, player value, position strength, lineup efficiency, matchup player contribution, and manager lineup tendency analytics (Epic 7, FFA-064 through FFA-070).

It makes live calls to the Sleeper API and to nflverse (via the cached providers already built in fantasy_analyzer.players) -- nothing here uses test fixtures. This is exploratory/reporting code, not library code: per AGENTS.md, notebooks are for exploration and are not covered by the unit test suite.

Prerequisites¶

This notebook needs a Jupyter kernel running the project's virtual environment, including the matplotlib dev extra used for the charts below:

.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"
.venv/bin/python -m ipykernel install --user --name fantasy-analyzer

Then select the fantasy-analyzer kernel for this notebook. The first run will download and cache nflverse's weekly player-stats file (.cache/nflverse/player_stats.csv) and the Sleeper player catalog (.cache/sleeper/players.json) -- subsequent runs reuse those caches.

Chart styling¶

A small, self-contained styling layer so every chart in this notebook reads as one system: a fixed categorical hue order (used only where color encodes identity, e.g. one team's actual-vs-optimal lines or a position breakdown), a single accent hue for plain magnitude/ranking bars, and a one-hue sequential ramp for the position-strength heatmap. Team-ranking bar charts deliberately do not try to give each of the league's 10 teams its own hue -- past ~8 series no fixed categorical order stays distinguishable, so identity there is carried by the axis labels instead, and color is just a single accent.

In [2]:
# Fixed categorical hue order (blue, orange, aqua, yellow, magenta, green,
# violet, red) -- assign by *identity* (e.g. position), never by rank, and
# never reuse a slot for something else within one chart.
CATEGORICAL = [
    "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100",
    "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#4a3aa7", "#e34948",
]
ACCENT = CATEGORICAL[0]
GOOD = "#0ca30c"
CRITICAL = "#d03b3b"

INK = "#0b0b0b"
INK_SECONDARY = "#52514e"
INK_MUTED = "#898781"
GRID = "#e1e0d9"
SURFACE = "#fcfcfb"

# Sequential single-hue (blue) ramp for magnitude encodings (heatmap cells).
SEQUENTIAL_BLUE = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "sequential_blue", ["#cde2fb", "#3987e5", "#0d366b"]
)

POSITION_ORDER = ["QB", "RB", "WR", "TE", "K", "DEF"]
POSITION_COLORS = dict(zip(POSITION_ORDER, CATEGORICAL))


def style_ax(ax, title=None, ylabel=None):
    """Apply this notebook's shared chart chrome to one axes."""
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.figure.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color(GRID)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID)
    ax.tick_params(colors=INK_SECONDARY, labelsize=9)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11, color=INK, loc="left", pad=8, weight="bold")
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=9, color=INK_SECONDARY)


def position_order_key(position: str) -> int:
    return POSITION_ORDER.index(position) if position in POSITION_ORDER else len(POSITION_ORDER)

3. Build the league foundation (Epics 2-6)¶

One LeagueSnapshot, the normalized season of matchups, and LeagueAnalytics -- everything league_walkthrough.ipynb demonstrates in depth. This notebook just builds them once and moves straight to the roster-level analysis; see that notebook for the per-metric walkthrough of each piece.

In [5]:
snapshot = load_league_snapshot(client, LEAGUE_ID)
summary = build_league_summary(snapshot, total_weeks=TOTAL_WEEKS)

boundaries = derive_season_boundaries(snapshot.league, total_weeks=TOTAL_WEEKS)
weeks = load_season_matchups(client, LEAGUE_ID, boundaries, season=snapshot.league.season)

outcomes = derive_season_outcomes(pairings)

    winners_bracket_raw=winners_bracket_raw,
    losers_bracket_raw=losers_bracket_raw,

4. Build the player-week fact table (FFA-060 through FFA-064)¶

The Epic 7 foundation every roster analysis below is built on: Sleeper's own weekly roster data (who was rostered, who started) joined against nflverse's raw weekly stats (via the Sleeper<->nflverse gsis_id crosswalk, FFA-062) and scored with this league's actual Sleeper scoring settings (FFA-063). One row per (week, rostered player) -- see players/player_week.py for the exact row universe and edge cases.

unsupported_scoring_keys matters here, not just in theory: this league's scoring settings lean heavily on tiered/bonus DEF and kicker categories (pts_allow_* bands, fgm_* distance bands, def_st_td, blk_kick, ...) plus a handful of offensive bonus/turnover categories (int, fum, sack, 2-point conversions) that nflverse's RAW_STAT_COLUMNS simply doesn't carry a matching raw stat for -- run the next cell and you'll see a non-empty, fairly long list. This is a real, material gap, not a formality: it means fantasy_points below understates real Sleeper scoring specifically for K and DEF, whose points are almost entirely made up of the missing tiered categories. Read every K/DEF number in this notebook (position strength, player value, roster composition) with that in mind -- offense-position numbers (QB/RB/WR/TE) are not affected, since their scoring categories (yardage, TDs, receptions) are all covered by nflverse's raw stats. Closing this gap would mean adding a K/DEF-specific stats source to the provider layer -- out of scope for this notebook.

In [6]:
player_catalog = get_players_cached(client)
id_crosswalk = build_id_crosswalk(player_catalog)
provider = NflverseWeeklyStatsProvider(id_crosswalk=id_crosswalk)

fact_table = build_player_week_fact_table(
    weeks, snapshot.teams_df, snapshot.players_df, provider, snapshot.scoring_settings
)
player_week_df = fact_table.player_week_df

if fact_table.unsupported_scoring_keys:
    print(f"WARNING -- unsupported scoring keys (points from these are NOT included): "
          f"{fact_table.unsupported_scoring_keys}")
else:
    print("Every scoring-settings category was mapped to a raw stat column.")

6. The team roster report¶

build_team_report(roster_id) is the "full end-to-end roster analysis for one team's season" -- it pulls every frame built above down to a single roster, in one place:

  • identity and final standing (Epic 3)
  • advanced league-analytics standing: power rank, all-play win rate, schedule luck, consistency, strength of schedule (Epic 6)
  • this roster's own players: every player who was ever on this roster_id this season, their games rostered/started, total and per-game fantasy points while on this roster -- distinct from player_season_df's player-level (not team-level) season totals, which can span a trade -- enriched with each player's league-wide replacement-value rank (FFA-068) for context
  • weekly lineup efficiency and the season roster-efficiency summary (FFA-067)
  • roster construction, bench allocation, and FLEX usage (FFA-070)
  • weekly matchup player contributions (FFA-069)

It returns a dict of scalars (for the cross-team comparison table in section 7) plus the underlying per-team DataFrames (for the deep-dive charts right below).

In [9]:
def build_team_report(roster_id: int) -> dict:
    """Full end-to-end roster analysis for one team's season.

    Combines standings/scoring, advanced league analytics, player-level
    value, weekly lineup efficiency, roster construction tendencies, and
    matchup player contributions -- everything built in sections 3-5 above,
    filtered down to a single roster_id. See the section 6 markdown cell
    for what each piece means.
    """
    team_row = snapshot.teams_df.loc[snapshot.teams_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    fantasy_team = team_row["display_name"]

    standings_row = standings_df.loc[standings_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    scoring_row = scoring_df.loc[scoring_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    power_row = power_df.loc[power_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    allplay_row = allplay_df.loc[allplay_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    luck_row = luck_df.loc[luck_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    consistency_row = consistency_df.loc[consistency_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    sos_row = sos_df.loc[sos_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].iloc[0]
    roster_eff_row = roster_efficiency_df.loc[roster_efficiency_df["roster_id"] == roster_id]
    start_sit_row = start_sit_df.loc[start_sit_df["roster_id"] == roster_id]

    team_player_weeks = player_week_df.loc[player_week_df["roster_id"] == roster_id].copy()
    # A handful of deep-bench/practice-squad players never resolve to a name
    # or position via either the provider join or the Sleeper catalog
    # fallback (see player_week.py's "Identity enrichment order") -- fall
    # back to the raw Sleeper player_id so they still get a readable label
    # instead of breaking the groupby key or a chart's string axis.
    team_player_weeks["player_name"] = team_player_weeks["player_name"].fillna(
        "Player " + team_player_weeks["sleeper_player_id"].astype(str)
    )
    team_player_weeks["position"] = team_player_weeks["position"].fillna("UNK")

    team_players = (
        team_player_weeks
        .groupby(["sleeper_player_id", "player_name", "position"], dropna=False)
        .agg(
            weeks_rostered=("week", "nunique"),
            weeks_started=("started", "sum"),
            total_points=("fantasy_points", "sum"),
            points_per_game=("fantasy_points", "mean"),
        )
        .reset_index()
        .sort_values("total_points", ascending=False)
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )
    team_players = team_players.merge(
        player_value_df[["sleeper_player_id", "value_rank", "points_above_replacement"]],
        on="sleeper_player_id",
        how="left",
    )

    weekly_efficiency = (
        lineup_efficiency_df.loc[lineup_efficiency_df["roster_id"] == roster_id]
        .sort_values("week")
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )
    position_summary = position_summary_df.loc[
        position_summary_df["fantasy_team"] == fantasy_team
    ].copy()
    position_summary["position_order"] = position_summary["position"].map(position_order_key)
    position_summary = position_summary.sort_values("position_order").reset_index(drop=True)

    roster_construction = roster_construction_df.loc[
        roster_construction_df["fantasy_team"] == fantasy_team
    ]
    contributions_team = contributions_df.loc[contributions_df["roster_id"] == roster_id]
    top_contributor_share = (
        contributions_team.loc[contributions_team["contribution_rank"] == 1, "share_of_team_points"]
        .mean()
    )

    placement_row = placements_df.loc[placements_df["roster_id"] == roster_id]

    return {
        "roster_id": roster_id,
        "fantasy_team": fantasy_team,
        "team_name": team_row["team_name"],
        "wins": int(standings_row["wins"]),
        "losses": int(standings_row["losses"]),
        "ties": int(standings_row["ties"]),
        "final_rank": int(standings_row["rank"]),
        "final_placement": (
            int(placement_row.iloc[0]["placement"]) if not placement_row.empty else None
        ),
        "points_per_game": scoring_row["points_per_game"],
        "power_rank": int(power_row["power_rank"]),
        "power_score": power_row["power_score"],
        "all_play_win_pct": allplay_row["all_play_win_pct"],
        "schedule_luck": luck_row["schedule_luck"],
        "consistency_cv": consistency_row["cv"],
        "sos_rank": int(sos_row["sos_rank"]),
        "efficiency_pct": (
            roster_eff_row.iloc[0]["efficiency_pct"] if not roster_eff_row.empty else float("nan")
        ),
        "points_left_on_bench": (
            roster_eff_row.iloc[0]["total_points_left_on_bench"]
            if not roster_eff_row.empty
            else float("nan")
        ),
        "suboptimal_starts_per_week": (
            start_sit_row.iloc[0]["suboptimal_starts_per_week"]
            if not start_sit_row.empty
            else float("nan")
        ),
        "top_player": team_players.iloc[0]["player_name"] if not team_players.empty else None,
        "top_player_points": (
            team_players.iloc[0]["total_points"] if not team_players.empty else float("nan")
        ),
        "top_contributor_share": top_contributor_share,
        "team_players": team_players,
        "weekly_efficiency": weekly_efficiency,
        "position_summary": position_summary,
        "roster_construction": roster_construction,
        "contributions": contributions_team,
    }

Worked example: one team, in full¶

Before running this across the whole league, here is the complete report for a single team, with every chart: weekly actual-vs-optimal lineup points (the shaded gap is points left on the bench each week), points per game by position, the top point-scorers actually rostered this season, and how much of the team's weekly score its single best player typically carried.

In [10]:
def plot_team_dashboard(report: dict, figsize=(15, 3.6)):
    """Render the four-panel chart dashboard for one team's report."""
    fig, (ax_eff, ax_pos, ax_players, ax_share) = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=figsize)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE)

    # Panel 1: weekly actual vs optimal lineup points, gap shaded.
    weekly = report["weekly_efficiency"]
    if not weekly.empty:
        ax_eff.plot(weekly["week"], weekly["actual_points"], color=CATEGORICAL[0],
                    linewidth=2, marker="o", markersize=4, label="Actual", zorder=3)
        ax_eff.plot(weekly["week"], weekly["optimal_points"], color=CATEGORICAL[1],
                    linewidth=2, linestyle="--", marker="o", markersize=4,
                    label="Optimal", zorder=3)
        ax_eff.fill_between(weekly["week"], weekly["actual_points"], weekly["optimal_points"],
                             color=CATEGORICAL[1], alpha=0.12, zorder=1)
        ax_eff.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="lower center",
                       ncol=2, labelcolor=INK_SECONDARY)
    style_ax(ax_eff, title="Actual vs. optimal lineup", ylabel="Points")
    ax_eff.set_xlabel("Week", fontsize=9, color=INK_SECONDARY)

    # Panel 2: points per game by position.
    pos = report["position_summary"]
    if not pos.empty:
        colors = [POSITION_COLORS.get(p, INK_MUTED) for p in pos["position"]]
        bars = ax_pos.bar(pos["position"], pos["points_per_game"], color=colors, width=0.6, zorder=3)
        ax_pos.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.1f", padding=2, fontsize=8, color=INK_SECONDARY)
    style_ax(ax_pos, title="Points/game by position", ylabel="Points per game")

    # Panel 3: top point-scorers actually rostered this season.
    top_players = report["team_players"].head(6).iloc[::-1]
    if not top_players.empty:
        bars = ax_players.barh(top_players["player_name"], top_players["total_points"],
                                color=ACCENT, height=0.6, zorder=3)
        ax_players.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.0f", padding=2, fontsize=8, color=INK_SECONDARY)
    style_ax(ax_players, title="Top point-scorers")
    ax_players.xaxis.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax_players.yaxis.grid(False)
    ax_players.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=8)

    # Panel 4: weekly top-contributor share of team points.
    contrib = report["contributions"]
    top_each_week = contrib.loc[contrib["contribution_rank"] == 1].sort_values("week")
    if not top_each_week.empty:
        ax_share.plot(top_each_week["week"], top_each_week["share_of_team_points"] * 100,
                       color=CATEGORICAL[6], linewidth=2, marker="o", markersize=4, zorder=3)
        ax_share.axhline(report["top_contributor_share"] * 100, color=INK_MUTED,
                          linewidth=1, linestyle=":", zorder=2)
    style_ax(ax_share, title="Top scorer's share of team points", ylabel="% of team points")
    ax_share.set_xlabel("Week", fontsize=9, color=INK_SECONDARY)
    ax_share.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter())

    fig.suptitle(
        f"{report['team_name']} ({report['fantasy_team']}) -- "
        f"{report['wins']}-{report['losses']}-{report['ties']}, "
        f"final rank {report['final_rank']}",
        fontsize=13, color=INK, weight="bold", x=0.01, ha="left",
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.90])
    return fig


example_roster_id = int(
    snapshot.teams_df.loc[snapshot.teams_df["owner_id"] == user_id, "roster_id"].iloc[0]
)
example_report = build_team_report(example_roster_id)

7. Apply the same analysis to every team¶

Running build_team_report once per roster_id produces the identical dashboard for every team in the league -- the exact analysis above, just looped. Each team's headline (record, points/game, efficiency) prints above its dashboard so the whole league can be scanned top to bottom; the scalar fields from every report are also collected into league_comparison_df for the cross-team charts in section 8.

In [11]:
reports = {}
comparison_rows = []

for roster_id in sorted(snapshot.teams_df["roster_id"]):
    report = build_team_report(roster_id)
    reports[roster_id] = report

    comparison_rows.append({
        key: value
        for key, value in report.items()
        if key not in ("team_players", "weekly_efficiency", "position_summary",
                        "roster_construction", "contributions")
    })

    display(Markdown(
        f"### {report['team_name']} ({report['fantasy_team']})\n"
        f"{report['wins']}-{report['losses']}-{report['ties']}, final rank "
        f"{report['final_rank']} &middot; {report['points_per_game']:.1f} pts/game &middot; "
        f"power rank #{report['power_rank']} &middot; lineup efficiency "
        f"{report['efficiency_pct']:.1%} &middot; top scorer **{report['top_player']}** "
        f"({report['top_player_points']:.0f} pts)"
    ))
    _ = plot_team_dashboard(report)
    plt.show()

league_comparison_df = pd.DataFrame(comparison_rows).sort_values("final_rank").reset_index(drop=True)
league_comparison_df

8. Comparing teams across the league¶

The per-team dashboards above are read one at a time; these charts put every team on the same axes. Team-ranking bar charts use a single accent hue -- with 10 teams there is no fixed categorical order that stays distinguishable, so identity is carried by the axis labels (see the styling note in section 1), and each bar is also directly labeled with its value.

Reminder from section 4: K/DEF fantasy points are understated all through this notebook (their real scoring is mostly tiered/bonus categories this league's provider pipeline doesn't carry), so treat the K/DEF columns/rows in the position-strength heatmap and the roster composition chart below as directional, not literal.

In [12]:
def ranked_bar(df, value_col, label_col, title, ylabel, fmt="%.1f",
               ascending=False, color=ACCENT, figsize=(11, 4)):
    """A single-hue, directly-labeled bar chart ranking every team by one metric."""
    ordered = df.sort_values(value_col, ascending=ascending)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    bars = ax.bar(ordered[label_col], ordered[value_col], color=color, width=0.6, zorder=3)
    ax.bar_label(bars, fmt=fmt, padding=2, fontsize=8, color=INK_SECONDARY)
    style_ax(ax, title=title, ylabel=ylabel)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=35)
    for label in ax.get_xticklabels():
        label.set_ha("right")
    fig.tight_layout()
    return fig

# Position strength heatmap: team x position, points per game, one sequential
# hue (magnitude, not identity) -- brighter/darker means more points.
pivot = position_summary_df.pivot_table(
    index="fantasy_team", columns="position", values="points_per_game", aggfunc="first"
)
pivot = pivot.reindex(columns=[p for p in POSITION_ORDER if p in pivot.columns])
pivot = pivot.loc[
    league_comparison_df.sort_values("final_rank")["fantasy_team"].tolist()
]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
im = ax.imshow(pivot.values, cmap=SEQUENTIAL_BLUE, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(pivot.columns)))
ax.set_xticklabels(pivot.columns, fontsize=9, color=INK_SECONDARY)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(pivot.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(pivot.index, fontsize=9, color=INK_SECONDARY)
ax.spines[:].set_visible(False)
ax.set_xticks([x - 0.5 for x in range(1, len(pivot.columns))], minor=True)
ax.set_yticks([y - 0.5 for y in range(1, len(pivot.index))], minor=True)
ax.grid(which="minor", color=SURFACE, linewidth=2)
ax.tick_params(which="minor", length=0)

for i in range(pivot.shape[0]):
    for j in range(pivot.shape[1]):
        value = pivot.values[i, j]
        if pd.notna(value):
            # Light text on the darkest cells, dark text elsewhere -- keeps
            # every label readable against the sequential ramp underneath it.
            text_color = SURFACE if value > pivot.values[~pd.isna(pivot.values)].mean() * 1.3 else INK
            ax.text(j, i, f"{value:.0f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8, color=text_color)

ax.set_title("Points per game by team and position (FFA-066)", fontsize=11, color=INK,
             loc="left", pad=10, weight="bold")
cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=8, colors=INK_SECONDARY)
cbar.outline.set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Lineup efficiency vs. scoring -- one dot per team, directly labeled (with
# only 10 points, a legend would cost more than it explains).
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
ax.scatter(league_comparison_df["points_per_game"], league_comparison_df["efficiency_pct"],
           color=ACCENT, s=70, zorder=3, edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1)
for _, row in league_comparison_df.iterrows():
    ax.annotate(row["fantasy_team"], (row["points_per_game"], row["efficiency_pct"]),
                textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, 4), fontsize=8, color=INK_SECONDARY)
ax.axvline(league_comparison_df["points_per_game"].mean(), color=GRID, linewidth=1, zorder=1)
ax.axhline(league_comparison_df["efficiency_pct"].mean(), color=GRID, linewidth=1, zorder=1)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
style_ax(ax, title="Scoring vs. lineup efficiency", ylabel="Lineup efficiency")
ax.set_xlabel("Points per game", fontsize=9, color=INK_SECONDARY)
fig.tight_layout()

# Roster composition: share of a team's rostered player-weeks spent at each
# position, 100%-stacked -- fixed position colors carry identity here since
# there are only 6 positions, well inside the categorical order's safe range.
composition = roster_construction_df.pivot_table(
    index="fantasy_team", columns="position", values="roster_share", aggfunc="first"
).fillna(0)
composition = composition.reindex(columns=[p for p in POSITION_ORDER if p in composition.columns])
composition = composition.loc[league_comparison_df.sort_values("final_rank")["fantasy_team"].tolist()]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5))
bottom = pd.Series(0.0, index=composition.index)
for position in composition.columns:
    values = composition[position]
    ax.bar(composition.index, values, bottom=bottom, label=position,
           color=POSITION_COLORS.get(position, INK_MUTED), width=0.6, zorder=3)
    bottom = bottom + values

ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, ncol=len(composition.columns), loc="upper center",
          bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.14), labelcolor=INK_SECONDARY)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
style_ax(ax, title="Roster composition -- share of rostered player-weeks by position (FFA-070)",
         ylabel="Share of roster")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=35)
for label in ax.get_xticklabels():
    label.set_ha("right")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Summary¶

  • build_team_report(roster_id) in section 6 composes the full Epic 1-7 pipeline -- league snapshot, matchup normalization, league analytics, the player-week fact table, player value, position strength, lineup efficiency, matchup player contribution, and lineup tendencies -- into one roster-level analysis.
  • Section 7 applies it to every roster_id in the league and collects the results into league_comparison_df.
  • Section 8 compares teams directly: power ranking, lineup efficiency, bench points wasted, schedule luck, position strength (heatmap), scoring vs. efficiency, and roster composition.
  • Every metric used here is defined and tested in its own module under src/fantasy_analyzer/analytics/ and src/fantasy_analyzer/players/ -- this notebook adds no new metrics, only composition and visualization.
